minutes.headline: Sewer Commission held off approving the 1700 Mass Ave betterment document until the final signed version arrives.
minutes.summary: The remote meeting heard homeowners at 1564 Mass Ave ask about tying into the sewer line instead of building a third septic system, and commissioners listed legal, technical and service-area hurdles. The board declined to approve the 1700 Mass Ave document without the final copy, approved the prior minutes with a correction, and covered billing, the station operator RFP, and the June 9 meeting with Woodard and Curran.

public_comment.topic: Homeowners at 1564 Mass Ave asked whether they could connect to the sewer line in front of their house rather than replace their septic system a third time.
Homeowner said both septic failures were the same, a leach field flooded with groundwater, and a new perc test would be needed.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the 5/12 meeting, later amended to include the corrections to the generator budget wording and the business manager report wording.

budget_items.what_was_said: Special legislation waives late charges and interest on invoices due between March and June 30 if paid by June 30; otherwise charges apply from the due date.
Irrigation meters must be upgraded to remote reading to keep the credit, and the program fee is due by early June.
A member and the homeowners noted that a typical septic system costs a substantial sum.
Fourth-quarter bills went out with a commitment amount stated, with inserts on the rate increase and pool fills.
Minutes corrected to say the generator budget includes repairs, and the commission has not spent more than that amount.
Two invoices for the pumping station operator were reported, one monthly and one covering January through April.
The business manager wants to tell the assessor and collector that no more betterments will be assessed once the document is final.

decisions.decision: The homeowners' attorney will research the grant restriction and sunset clause, the business manager will email a private extension checklist, and the commission will regroup afterward.
The commission agreed to wait for the final signed document from the selectman before approving the 1700 Mass Ave matter.
The June 9 meeting with Woodard and Curran will stay remote at 5:00 p.m.
The station operator RFP will be advertised widely, beyond past venues, with outreach to likely bidders.
The generator maintenance work will use three quotes rather than an RFP, after the new vendor is selected.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission agreed to wait for the final signed 1700 Mass Ave betterment document from the selectman before approving it.
Homeowners at 1564 Mass Ave asked to tie into the sewer line instead of building a third septic system; commissioners raised legal, technical and service-area hurdles.
The homeowners' attorney will research the grant restriction and sunset clause, and the commission will regroup afterward.
The commission approved the 5/12 minutes with a correction stating the generator budget includes repairs.
The station operator RFP will be advertised widely, and the June 9 meeting with Woodard and Curran will stay remote at 5:00 p.m.

why_it_matters: A sewer connection for 1564 Mass Ave depends on grant, sunset-clause and service-area rules, which decide whether properties outside the current sewer area can connect, instead of paying for a new septic system.
Sewer bills carry late-charge relief only for invoices paid by June 30, and a final betterment document would end new betterments on quarterly invoices.
